desk.headline: HEPS up 7% to 79c even as income slips 2% to R5.43bn on weaker slots; interim dividend held at 15c; October and November trading tough

other.label: Casinos revenue
other.change: -3%; casino adjusted EBITDA (excl. Theme Park) -6%, Theme Park EBITDA -37%

other.label: Net debt and guarantees
other.change: down R810m from R6.80bn at 30 Sep 2025

results: HEPS rose 7% to 79c from 74c, although headline earnings fell 2% to R757m.
Income dropped 2% to R5.43bn and adjusted EBITDA fell 4% to R1.65bn as slot machine revenue declined.
Casinos revenue slipped 3% to R4bn; Gold Reef City's Theme Park EBITDA fell 37% after a strike and intimidation at the casino and park.
Online betting was the bright spot, with revenue up 43% to R193m, while Bingo stayed difficult and hotel room revenue grew.
Net debt fell to R5.99bn, and the interim dividend was kept at 15c.

guidance.summary: No earnings targets. The group says October and November trading was particularly tough; it is refinancing R4.45bn of facilities due in 2027 and expects lower debt to keep cutting finance costs, partly offset by higher interest rates.

points: CEO Chris du Toit said October and November were particularly tough trading months after the period.
He called approvals for a new casino in the Helderberg area of the Western Cape positive for future growth.
He said falling net debt will keep reducing finance costs.
Bingo is moving to smaller, cheaper sites, and illegal online gambling and a possible casino smoking ban remain concerns.
call.source: The National (25 Nov 2026) and Sunday World (25 Nov 2026) coverage of the results

watch: Whether trading recovers over the festive season after a weak October and November.
Progress on the R4.45bn refinancing and the Helderberg casino project.
Recovery at Gold Reef City after the industrial action, and proposed tobacco rules for casino smoking areas.
